provisional_canonical_claim: Let M be an o-minimal expansion of a dense linear order and let f be a definable unary function on an interval. The domain admits a finite partition into points and intervals such that on every interval piece f is continuous and is either constant or strictly monotone.
domain_and_universes: Universes u v w; a first-order language L.{u,v} with a distinguished order relation; a carrier M : Type w with a compatible L-structure and dense linear order without endpoints; the order topology; parameters from the whole carrier; a definable domain and unary function with definable restricted graph.
quantifiers: parameter set or tuple, subject to the source convention
hypotheses: the order on M is dense, linear, and without endpoints if required by the selected source
the L-structure is o-minimal: every definable unary subset is a finite union of points and intervals
the graph and domain of f are definable under the selected parameter convention
conclusion: A finite pairwise-disjoint partition of the domain into singleton or order-convex pieces on which f is continuous and constant, strictly increasing, or strictly decreasing.

alternate_encodings.target: a finite exceptional set whose complementary interval components each carry one continuity/monotonicity behavior
alternate_encodings.relationship: intended equivalent to an explicit finite cell partition after checked transport

alternate_encodings.target: the defining one-dimensional finite-union-of-points-and-intervals property alone
alternate_encodings.relationship: definition/premise only, not a substitute for the provisional monotonicity conclusion
